title: A finitely generated extension whose p-th powers preserve linear independence is separably generated
statement: Let $p$ be a prime number, let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p$ and let $K/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] that is finitely generated, i.e. $K=k(a_1,\dots,a_n)$ for finitely many $a_1,\dots,a_n\in K$. Assume that for all pairwise distinct $b_1,\dots,b_m\in K$ ($m\ge0$) that are linearly independent over $k$ (no relation $\sum_ic_ib_i=0$ with $c_i\in k$ not all zero), the elements $b_1^p,\dots,b_m^p$ are linearly independent over $k$ (no relation $\sum_ic_ib_i^p=0$ with $c_i\in k$ not all zero). Then $K$ is separably generated over $k$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension] (1): there are finitely many $x_1,\dots,x_r\in K$ forming a transcendence basis of $K/k$ [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis] such that $K/k(x_1,\dots,x_r)$ is separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension].
